conclusion: Authoritative current evidence answers both fee questions. Utah BCI's live FAQ states a nonrefundable $65 application fee and a $65 per-case certificate fee for eligible conviction, plea-in-abeyance, and special certificates; it states no issuance fee for dismissals, acquittals, or declinations. The current BCI application PDF was last updated 2026-03-16 and independently states the $65 application fee and court-obtained indigency waiver path. Utah Courts' fee table is effective May 6, 2026 and lists expungement filing at $150 in District Court and $135 in Justice Court. The five held ancillary PDFs identify their printed titles and revisions. 1149XX and 1169XX print Board approval dates; 1044XX, 1146XX, and 1148XX print revision dates only, with no approval-date line. No counsel or owner approval is implied.

findings.question: BCI application fee
findings.scopeAndExceptions: The current application says the fee is $65 and nonrefundable. Its instructions say an applicant claiming indigency must submit the fee-waiver form before processing; the waiver form is returned with certificates if eligible.

findings.question: Special-certificate issuance fee
findings.answer: $65 for each eligible special certificate/case, charged after review/eligibility.
findings.scopeAndExceptions: The live BCI FAQ expressly includes special certificates in the $65 per-case charge. The BCI criteria flyer, updated January 2025, independently says an additional $65 fee per certificate applies to conviction, plea-in-abeyance, or special certificates; no fee applies to declined, dismissed-without-plea-in-abeyance, or acquitted cases. The FAQ says any indigency waiver for certificate and court fees must be obtained from the court.

findings.question: Utah expungement petition filing fee
findings.scopeAndExceptions: Utah Courts' fee page states the table is effective May 6, 2026 and lists Expungement under Utah Code §78A-2-301(1)(i)(i). The current District and Justice cover sheets carry the same effective revision date and matching amounts. This is the filing fee before any court fee waiver; it does not answer eligibility or other service/copy charges.
